# `silk/compress/tar`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write tar archives held in memory.

## When to use
Use a [`TarReader`](#TarReader) to unpack a `.tar` file, or a `.tar.gz` file after you decode it with
`silk.compress.inflate`. Open the archive with [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open) and call [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next)
until it returns none. Use a [`TarWriter`](#TarWriter) to make one: add members with [`TarWriter.file`](#TarWriter.impl.file) and
[`TarWriter.directory`](#TarWriter.impl.directory), then take the bytes with [`TarWriter.finish`](#TarWriter.impl.finish), and compress them with
`silk.compress.deflate` for a `.tar.gz`. This module does not compress or decompress.

## Details
The reader understands ustar, GNU, and pax archives: the ustar `prefix` field, GNU long names,
pax `path` records, and base-256 sizes. It does not allocate, and every member it returns
borrows the archive. Each header's checksum is checked. A member's path is checked before the
member is returned: an absolute path, a backslash, a NUL, or a `..` segment refuses the archive, so a
caller that joins a path to a directory and creates no links never writes outside it. Empty and
`.` segments are allowed, because `tar -C dir .` writes paths such as `./include/x.h`.

The writer writes ustar headers with fixed metadata: modification time 0, owner and group 0
with no names, and mode 644, or 755 for an executable file or a directory. A path longer than
100 bytes goes in the ustar `prefix` field when it splits at a `/`, else in a pax `path`
record. The same members in the same order give the same bytes on every host, so a checksum of
the archive names its content.

## Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) from [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next) when a header is corrupt, the archive ends inside a
  member, or a path is unsafe.
- [`TarError`](#TarError) from [`TarWriter.file`](#TarWriter.impl.file) and [`TarWriter.directory`](#TarWriter.impl.directory) when a path is one the
  reader would refuse: empty, absolute, ending in `/`, or with a backslash, a NUL or a `..`
  segment.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.compress.tar {TarError, TarKind, TarMember, TarReader}
import silk.core.option {Option}
import silk.core.result {Result}

// Counts the regular files of `archive`, or answers -1 when it is not a valid tar archive.
fn files(archive: &[u8]) -> i32 {
  let mut reader = TarReader.open(archive)
  let mut count = 0
  while true {
    match TarReader.next(&mut reader) {
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Success {value} => match move value {
        Option<TarMember>.Some {value: member} => { if member.kind == TarKind.File { count = count + 1 } }
        Option<TarMember>.None => { return count }
      }
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Failure {..} => { return -1 }
    }
  }
  return count
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let empty: [u8; 1024] = [0; 1024]
  return files(&empty)
}
```

### Write an archive and read it back
```silk
import silk.collections.bytes {Bytes}
import silk.compress.tar {TarError, TarMember, TarReader, TarWriter}
import silk.core.effect {Effect}
import silk.core.option {Option}
import silk.core.result {Result}
import silk.mem.allocator {Allocator, OutOfMemoryError}

effect fn archive() -> Bytes ! TarError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut writer = TarWriter.make()
  run TarWriter.directory(&mut writer, b"app/bin")
  run TarWriter.file(&mut writer, b"app/bin/run", b"#!/bin/sh\n", true)
  run TarWriter.file(&mut writer, b"app/README", b"hello\n", false)
  return run TarWriter.finish(move writer)
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! TarError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let bytes = run archive() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut reader = TarReader.open(Bytes.asSlice(&bytes))
  let mut members = 0
  while true {
    match TarReader.next(&mut reader) {
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Success {value} => match move value {
        Option<TarMember>.Some {..} => { members = members + 1 }
        Option<TarMember>.None => { break }
      }
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Failure {..} => { return 1 }
    }
  }
  return if members == 3 { 0 } else { 2 }
}
```

<a id="TarMember"></a>

## `TarMember`

```silk
pub struct TarMember<'a>
```

One member of a tar archive: its checked path, its kind, and its content.

### Details
The member's path is `prefix/name`, `name` alone when `prefix` is empty, or `prefix` alone when
`name` is empty, as ustar writes a long directory path. A GNU long name or a
pax `path` record comes back as `name` with an empty `prefix`. The slices borrow the archive
given to [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open).

<a id="TarMember.prefix"></a>

### Field `prefix`

```silk
pub prefix: &'a [u8]
```

The ustar `prefix` field, or empty.

<a id="TarMember.name"></a>

### Field `name`

```silk
pub name: &'a [u8]
```

The rest of the path, without the trailing `/` a directory may carry.

<a id="TarMember.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`

```silk
pub kind: TarKind
```

Whether the member is a file, a directory, a link, or something else.

<a id="TarMember.executable"></a>

### Field `executable`

```silk
pub executable: bool
```

Whether the member is a file whose mode has an execute permission bit.

<a id="TarMember.link"></a>

### Field `link`

```silk
pub link: &'a [u8]
```

The target of a symbolic or hard link from the header's 100-byte link field, or empty. GNU
long link names and pax `linkpath` records are not read.

<a id="TarMember.content"></a>

### Field `content`

```silk
pub content: &'a [u8]
```

The bytes of a regular file. It is empty for a directory or a link.

<a id="TarReader"></a>

## `TarReader`

```silk
pub struct TarReader<'a>
```

A position in a tar archive held in memory.

### When to use
Make one with [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open) and call [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next) until it returns none.

### Details
The reader does not allocate and borrows the archive. It stops at the first all-zero block or at
the end of the bytes. After a failure, discard the reader.

<a id="TarReader.impl"></a>

<a id="TarReader.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub fn next(self: &mut TarReader<'a>) -> Result<Option<TarMember<'a>>, TarError>
```

Returns the next member in archive order, or none at the end-of-archive blocks or the end of
the bytes. GNU long-name and pax headers are read as part of the member they name.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `Truncated` when the archive ends inside a header or a member,
  `BadHeader` when a checksum or number is invalid, and `UnsafePath` when the member's path
  is absolute, holds a backslash or a NUL, or has a `..` segment.

<a id="TarWriter"></a>

## `TarWriter`

```silk
pub struct TarWriter
```

A tar archive being written in memory, one member at a time.

### When to use
Make one with [`TarWriter.make`](#TarWriter.impl.make), add members with [`TarWriter.file`](#TarWriter.impl.file) and
[`TarWriter.directory`](#TarWriter.impl.directory) in the order the archive should list them, and take the archive with
[`TarWriter.finish`](#TarWriter.impl.finish).

### Details
The writer writes ustar headers with fixed metadata: modification time zero, owner and group
zero with empty names, and mode 644 for a file, 755 for an executable file or a directory. The
same members in the same order therefore always give the same bytes, on any host. A path
longer than the 100-byte name field is split into the ustar prefix and name at a `/` when it
fits, and is otherwise written in a pax `path` record. A file of 8 GiB or more records its size
in base-256. [`TarReader`](#TarReader) reads every archive the writer makes.

<a id="TarWriter.impl.file"></a>

### Method `file`

```silk
pub effect fn file(self: &mut Self, path: &[u8], content: &[u8], executable: bool) -> ()
    ! TarError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds the regular file `path` holding `content`, with mode 755 when `executable` and 644
otherwise.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `UnsafePath` when `path` is empty, absolute, ends in `/`, or holds a
  backslash, a NUL, or a `..` segment. Nothing is added.
- `OutOfMemoryError` when the archive cannot grow.

Adds the directory `path`, with mode 755. Write it without a trailing `/`.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `UnsafePath` when `path` is empty, absolute, ends in `/`, or holds a
  backslash, a NUL, or a `..` segment. Nothing is added.
- `OutOfMemoryError` when the archive cannot grow.
